items.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: B.B. King doing the “Three O’clock Blues”

ctx.x: Well it’s interesting, but I was shuffling through some LPs the other night because my wife had to clean out a certain section, you know, “We’ve got to clean out, there’s too much dust over there, get these LPs out” and it happened to be the end of V through Z. And so I was looking through them naturally after we got them out. And here was Joe Williams, it’s a Savoy LP, I don’t know if it’s been re-issued on CD, and it had some of his early work, pre-Basie. And there’s a version of “Every Day” on there and it…

that really helped establish that band because the R & B shows, the D.J.s were playing Basie and the young kids started to listen to this band. It wasn’t played just on jazz shows, because of some of the things they did. And I remember because I was working for Prestige Records at the time and we had to monitor Tommy “Dr. Jive” Smalls. He was the D.J. on WWRL out in Long Island. And they were slipping him five or ten dollars to play some of the Prestige numbers, right? So we had to, while we were packing boxes…
